title: Windows website, 2013
lede: The Windows 8 consumer site: a black header, a photo hero, and a full-width yellow band with large dark type.
summary: Black header, flat cyan button, and a solid yellow band with large dark gray headline. April 2013.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 from the Wayback Machine copy of 1 April 2013, and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens. Nothing covers the page. Segoe UI is not installed on the capture machine, so text that the archive did not serve as a web font renders in a fallback sans-serif.

styles.note: Clear: a flat black header, a square cyan button, and a full-width solid yellow band; the headings are heavier than Metro’s usual light weight.

observed: A black header holds the cyan Windows logo, uppercase white navigation, and a dark gray search field.

A photograph of a family on a beach fills the hero, with a tablet showing the Windows 8 Start screen tiles. The headline “Meet Windows 8” is large dark gray type; a square cyan “Take a look” button sits below.
A full-width solid yellow band follows, with the headline “Positioned for success” in large dark gray type and a photo of a laptop.
interpretation: Measured: 39% of screenshot pixels are saturated, in 7 hue groups (partly from the photograph); no radius, shadow, or gradient. Large headings measure weight 600, so the capture fails the heading-weight range; the lower screens were measured but are not in the screenshot.
borrow: Alternate photo bands with solid color bands of the same height, and keep the same headline treatment on both.

images.alt: Windows home page of April 2013: a black header with the Windows logo, a photo hero of a family and a tablet showing the Start screen with the headline Meet Windows 8 and a cyan button, and a yellow band with the headline Positioned for success.
images.caption: First viewport of the [Wayback Machine copy of windows.microsoft.com, 1 April 2013](https://web.archive.org/web/20130401135628/http://windows.microsoft.com/en-US/windows/home).
